 FORWARD-LOOKING INFORMATION
Fortis includes forward-looking information in this presentation within the meaning of applicable Canadian securities laws and forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995
(collectively referred to as "forward-looking information"). Forward-looking information reflects expectations of Fortis management regarding future growth, results of operations, performance and business prospects and
opportunities. Wherever possible, words such as anticipates, believes, budgets, could, estimates, expects, forecasts, intends, may, might, plans, projects, schedule, should, target, will, would, and the negative of these terms, and
other similar terminology or expressions have been used to identify the forward-looking information, which includes, without limitation: forecast Capital Expenditures for 2026 and 2027-2031; expected timing, outcome, and impact of
legal and regulatory proceedings; forecast five-year CAGR to 2031; annual dividend growth guidance through 2031; forecast Rate Base for 2026 through 2031; forecast three-year CAGR to 2029; the expectation that the proportion of
ITC's FERC-regulated assets in the Corporation's consolidated Rate Base will increase during the Capital Plan period; expected nature, timing, benefits, and costs of certain opportunities above and beyond the Capital Plan at ITC,
including investments associated with the MISO LRTP Tranche 2.1 projects, other MISO LRTP and MTEP projects, and customer connections associated with load growth; expected in-service dates and total cost of the MARS project;
expected nature, timing, benefits, and costs of certain opportunities above and beyond the Capital Plan at UNS Energy, including investments associated with load growth for new and existing customers, integrated resource plans,
and FERC-regulated transmission; expected timing and resources for TEP to serve load pursuant to an energy supply agreement with its data center customer; estimated costs of incremental generation and associated transmission
investments associated with the approximately 800 MW high-growth scenario in TEP's IRP; planned resource additions under TEP's and UNS Electric's base case IRPs; projected average system cost per kWh under various scenarios
included in TEP's IRP; TEP's planned retirement of coal-fired generation by 2032; expected nature, timing, benefits, and costs of certain opportunities above and beyond the Capital Plan at FortisBC, including investments associated
with the Tilbury LNG Expansion post-2031, Regional Transmission Pipeline Expansion, and customer and load growth in the Okanagan electric service territory; estimated potential incremental capital above and beyond the Capital
Plan; expected and potential impacts on rates associated with various affordability initiatives, including O&M savings targets at Central Hudson, beneficial load growth at ITC Midwest and TEP, capital optimization related to the UNS
Springerville Natural Gas Generation, and rate benefits associated with LNG projects at FortisBC and the Eagle Mountain Pipeline Project; expected sources of funding for the Capital Plan, including common equity provided through
the DRIP at current participation levels; the expectation of a consistent capital structure over the planning period; the expectation that the funding plan supports existing investment-grade credit ratings; planned re-establishment of
the short-form base shelf prospectus and ATM Program; expected issuances of common shares under ATM Program over next 12 months; forecast credit metrics for 2026 and 2027-2031; forecast Capital Expenditures for 2027-2031
by business unit; forecast capital expenditures for pre-2027, 2027-2031, post-2031, total project cost and estimated completion dates of Major Capital Projects, including ITC MISO LRTP – Tranche 1, ITC MISO LRTP – Tranche 2.1, ITC
Big Cedar Load Expansion, UNS Transmission Project at TEP, UNS Gas Generation Project at UNS Electric, UNS Springerville Natural Gas Generation, FortisBC Tilbury 1B Project, FortisBC LNG Storage Tank Expansion, FortisBC AMI
Project, and FortisBC Eagle Mountain Pipeline Project; expected construction timing of Tilbury 1B; expected stakeholder consultation related to Tilbury Phase 2 LNG Expansion; potential additional capacity of, ability to supply domestic
or bulk LNG export markets from, and expected staged development of the Tilbury Phase 2 Liquefaction Expansion; forecast Rate Base for 2026 through 2031 and five-year CAGR to 2031 by business unit; estimated impact of the U.S.
dollar-to-Canadian dollar exchange rate, inclusive of hedging activities, on the Capital Plan and EPS; the Corporation's commitment to a coal-free generation mix by 2032; the Corporation's 2050 net-zero greenhouse gas emissions
target; and forecast debt maturities for 2027-2036.

Forward-looking information involves significant risks, uncertainties, and assumptions. Certain material factors or assumptions have been applied in drawing the conclusions contained in the forward-looking information including,
without limitation: the successful execution of the Capital Plan; no material capital project or financing cost overrun; sufficient human resources to deliver service and execute the Capital Plan; the realization of additional opportunities
beyond the Capital Plan; no significant variability in interest rates; no material changes in the assumed U.S. dollar-to-Canadian dollar exchange rate; the Board exercising its discretion to declare dividends, taking into account the
financial performance and condition of the Corporation; reasonable legal and regulatory decisions and the expectation of regulatory stability; no significant operational disruptions or environmental liability or upset; the continued
ability to maintain the performance of the electricity and gas systems; no severe and prolonged economic downturn; sufficient liquidity and capital resources; the ability to hedge exposures to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates,
natural gas prices and electricity prices; the continued availability of natural gas, fuel, coal and electricity supply; continuation of power supply and capacity purchase contracts; no significant changes in government energy policies,
environmental laws and regulations that could have a material negative impact; maintenance of adequate insurance coverage; the ability to obtain and maintain licenses and permits; retention of existing service areas; no significant
changes in tax laws and the continued tax deferred treatment of earnings from the Corporation's foreign operations; continued maintenance of information technology infrastructure and no material breach of cybersecurity;
continued favourable relations with Indigenous Peoples; and favourable labour relations.

Fortis cautions readers that a number of factors could cause actual results, performance or achievements to differ materially from the results discussed or implied in the forward-looking information. These factors should be
considered carefully, and undue reliance should not be placed on the forward-looking information. For additional information with respect to certain of these risks or factors, reference should be made to the continuous disclosure
materials filed from time to time by the Corporation with Canadian securities regulatory authorities and the Securities and Exchange Commission. All forward-looking information herein is given as of the date of this presentation.
Fortis disclaims any intention or obligation to update or revise any forward-looking information, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise.

Unless otherwise specified, all financial information is in Canadian dollars and rate base refers to midyear rate base.

Note: U.S. dollar-denominated five-year Capital Plan and forecast rate base converted at a forecast USD:CAD foreign exchange rate of 1.35 for 2027-2031.
